summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell activation disorder was admitted after using her EpiPen for a flare triggered by rain, presenting with chest pain, dyspnea, and back pain following a recent syncopal fall. She reported new right lower quadrant and back pain, along with two episodes of urinary incontinence. Imaging showed no acute abdominal or spinal pathology, and labs were stable. Her midodrine was restarted to prevent further syncope, and she was treated with IV Benadryl and a short steroid course for mast cell flare. Symptoms improved during the hospitalization, with resolution of dyspnea and reduced pain. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, including reduced ranitidine and doxepin, a new Adderall formulation, and a switch from cefuroxime to nitrofurantoin for UTI prophylaxis. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider and a new allergist specializing in mast cell disorders.
problems: Other specified disorders involving the immune mechanism
